title: Human Brain Sequential Extraction (Tau)
author: Michael X. Henderson
materials: Thaw bag(s) of brain tissue On ice .
Move brain to petri dish and weigh it.
Bleach vacuum flask and rinse out.

steps.title: Clean homogenizers and ultracentrifuge tubes
steps.instruction: Clean 100 mL or 40 mL glass homogenizers and pestles (A and B) with 70 % ethanol, wrap in foil, autoclave; clean ultracentrifuge tubes and caps with 70 % ethanol and dry.

steps.title: Prepare ultracentrifuge and ice
steps.instruction: Turn on the Optima L‑100 XP ultracentrifuge, set temperature to 4 °C, turn the vacuum on, and verify that Ti‑45 and Ti‑70 rotors are available (room 5124). Fill two buckets with wet ice.

steps.title: Freeze tissue and record data
steps.instruction: Transfer brain tissue to a –20 °C freezer the night before to speed thaw; note case number, weight of the dish for gray‑matter weighing, and ensure sufficient protease inhibitor, phosphatase inhibitor, and DTT are on hand.

steps.title: Fix a representative tissue piece
steps.instruction: After thaw, remove meninges and blood vessels, cut one thin representative piece, and place it into a 15 mL conical containing 10 % neutral‑buffered formalin (NBF) labeled with the case number for fixation and later IHC.

steps.title: Dissect gray matter
steps.instruction: In ice‑cold PBS, carefully separate gray matter from white matter, transfer the gray matter to a petri dish on ice, and weigh it.

steps.title: Prepare extraction buffer per gram
steps.instruction: Prepare 30 mL Extraction Buffer for each gram of gray matter; to ice‑cold Base Buffer add Complete protease inhibitor (1 tablet per 50 mL), phosphatase inhibitors 2 & 3 (1 : 100), PMSF 0.1 mM (1 : 5000), and DTT 2 mM (1 : 500).

steps.title: First homogenization and low‑speed spin
steps.instruction: Add 9 volumes of Extraction Buffer to a homogenizer tube, cut gray matter into small bits, and transfer bits with buffer; homogenize with pestle A until it moves easily, then with pestle B for three × 25 strokes; save 200 µL as Total Homogenate; pour homogenate evenly into Ti‑45 tubes (≈50 mL/tube), balance tubes within 0.1 g; spin at 11 300 rpm (≈10 000 × g) for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect first supernatant (Sup 1)
steps.instruction: Filter the supernatant through a double‑layer kimwipe placed in a funnel into a 50 mL conical and save 200 µL as Sup 1.

steps.title: Second homogenization of pellet
steps.instruction: Add 9 volumes of Extraction Buffer to the pellet‑containing centrifuge tube, transfer the pellet to a new homogenizer, homogenize with pestle A until easy, then pestle B for three × 25 strokes; save 200 µL as Pel 1; pour homogenate into Ti‑45 tubes, balance within 0.1 g; spin at 11 300 rpm (≈10 000 × g) for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect second supernatant (Sup 2) and add sarkosyl
steps.instruction: During the spin, transfer Sup 1 to a beaker with a stir bar and add sarkosyl to a final 1 % (1 / 27); after the spin, filter the new supernatant through a double‑layer kimwipe into a 50 mL conical and save 200 µL as Sup 2; combine Sup 1 and Sup 2 in the beaker, add sarkosyl to a final 1 % (1 / 27), save 200 µL as Total Sup; stir Total Sup at room temperature for 1 – 1.5 h.

steps.title: Third homogenization and high‑speed spin
steps.instruction: Add Extraction Buffer to the pellet tube (use the same volume as Sup 2), transfer the pellet to a homogenizer, homogenize as before, and save 200 µL equivalent as Pel 2 (dilute if volume smaller); add Total Sup to Ti‑45 tubes, balance within 0.1 g, and spin at 40 000 rpm (≈125 000 × g) for 1 h 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect Sarkosyl supernatant and wash pellet
steps.instruction: Pipette the supernatant into a beaker (myelin floats) and remove myelin with a pipette; save 200 µL as Sark Sup (pellet should be tight, sticky, red‑brown); use a vacuum to aspirate remaining liquid around the pellet (do not insert tubing); add 10 mL DPBS to each tube and vacuum‑remove; add 2 mL DPBS and vacuum‑remove; add 1 mL DPBS, pipette toward the pellet with a cut P1000 tip until loosened, then transfer the pellet to a Ti‑70 tube with a transfer pipette, avoiding loss.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet and high‑speed spin
steps.instruction: Use a cut P1000 tip to pipette up/down and resuspend the pellet; add DPBS to reach the tube’s maximum volume, balance within 0.1 g; spin at 50 000 rpm (≈18 000 × g) for 30 min at 4 °C; save 200 µL of the supernatant as DPBS wash and remove the remaining supernatant by vacuum.

steps.title: Final DPBS wash and vortex
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL DPBS per gram of tissue to the pellet, loosen with a cut P1000 tip, break up as much as possible without up/down pipetting, and transfer to 1.5 mL tubes (pellet may stick to tip); vortex briefly and spin in a tabletop centrifuge at 1 000 × g for 1 min.

steps.title: Decontaminate equipment
steps.instruction: Bleach all homogenizers, tools, and tubes (use only soap for metal lids); rinse centrifuge tubes for 10 min after bleaching.

steps.title: Process fixed brain for paraffin embedding
steps.instruction: Move the fixed brain to leaching buffer and a cassette for paraffin embedding; spin in a tabletop centrifuge at 1 000 × g for 1 min at 4 °C; pass the suspension repeatedly through a 27 G ½‑inch needle (start with a 19 G 1½‑inch needle if clumps are large); if needed, centrifuge at 1 000 × g for 1 min to bring material to the tube bottom.

steps.title: Resuspend Sarkosyl pellet and low‑speed spin
steps.instruction: Transfer the resuspended Sark Pel to an autoclaved 1.5 mL Beckman ultracentrifuge tube; add 100 µL DPBS, resuspend well, and save 30 µL as Sark Pel; balance tubes within 0.1 g and spin in the OptimaMAX‑TL (room 5124) TLA100.3 rotor at 45 000 rpm (≈80 000 × g) for 30 min at 4 °C; remove supernatant, add 100 µL DPBS per gram tissue to the pellet, vortex; freeze or continue processing the pellet.

steps.title: Sonicate Sarkosyl pellet and second high‑g spin
steps.instruction: Sonicate the pellet with 20 × 1 s pulses using a hand sonicator; balance tubes within 0.1 g and spin in the OptimaMAX‑TL at 45 000 rpm (≈80 000 × g) for 30 min at 4 °C; transfer the supernatant to a new tube as High‑g Sup.

steps.title: Resuspend High‑g pellet and sonicate
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet with 20 % of its volume of DPBS (e.g., 700 µL Sup → 140 µL DPBS); sonicate on ice with 90‑120 × 1 s pulses; save 10 µL as High‑g Pel; transfer the resuspended High‑g pellet to a 1.5 mL tube and spin at 10 000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect Low‑g supernatant (final tau)
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant with a sterile pipette tip to a 1.5 mL tube and save 20 µL as Low‑g Sup (contains enriched pathological tau).

steps.title: Final pellet resuspension and storage
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of DPBS to the remaining pellet, sonicate with 30 × 1 s pulses using a hand sonicator to resuspend, and save 200 µL of this pellet as Log g Pel.
